questions.question: Three years ago, the ratio of the age of A to that of B was 8 ∶ 9. Five years hence, the ratio of the age of A to that of B will be 10 ∶ 11. If at present, C is 8 years younger than A, then the ratio of the present age of B to that of C is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of ages of A and B (3 years ago) = 8 : 9

Ratio of ages of A and B (5 years hence) = 10 : 11

C = A - 8 (C is 8 years younger than A)

**Calculation:**

C = A - 8 ----(1)

Ratio of ages of A and B at present = 8x + 3/9x + 3 = 10x - 5/11x - 5 ----(2)

⇒ 8x + 3/9x + 3 = 10x - 5/11x - 5 

∴ By cross multiplication,

⇒ 88x² - 7x -15 = 90x² -15x -15

⇒ 2x² - 8x = 0

⇒ x(2x - 8) = 0

⇒ x = 0, x = 4 (possible value)

Putting x = 4 in equation (2) we get,

A present age = (8x + 3) = 35 years 

B present age = (9x + 3) = 39 years

From equation (1) we get,

C present age = 27 years

Ratio of present ages of B and C = 39/27 = 13 : 9

**∴ The present ratio of B and C is 13 : 9.**

Ratio of ages of persons remains same at any given year.

questions.question: A semi-circular field of radius 14 m needs to be fenced with a wire. Find the length of wire required.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **semi-circular field**, the fencing required is the **perimeter**.

**Perimeter** of semi-circle = (π + 2) × r

Using π = 22/7 and r = 14 m:

Perimeter = (22/7 + 2) × 14 = (36/7) × 14 = 36 × 2 = 72 m

**∴ The correct answer is 72 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Radius (r)** of the semi-circular field = 14 m

**Formula Used:**

**Length of wire** = **Perimeter of semi-circle** = **Circumference of arc** + **Diameter**

**Perimeter** = πr + 2r

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/854d5a24af8bd3912ca238376b500999e6c6e2febfede7be279262f5c2da4d6e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Length of wire** = (22/7 × 14) + (2 × 14)

⇒ **Length of wire** = (22 × 2) + 28

⇒ **Length of wire** = 44 + 28

⇒ **Length of wire** = 72 m

**∴ The correct answer is 72 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Semi-circle

The space occupied by the semi-circle is half the area of a full circle: Area = (1/2) × πr².

Full Circle Perimeter

The total boundary length or circumference of a complete circle is given by 2πr.

Quadrant of a Circle

For a quarter circle, the perimeter includes the arc length and two radii: Perimeter = (πr/2) + 2r.</p

questions.question: What will be the difference between simple and compound interest at 10% per annum on a sum of Rs 1,000 after 4 years?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal sum (P) = Rs 1,000.

Rate of interest per annum (r) = 10%.

Time period (n) = 4 years.

**Formula used:**

SI = (P × R × T)/100

CI = P[(1 + R/100)ⁿ - 1]

**Calculation:**

SI = (P × R × T)/100

⇒ (1000 × 10 × 4)/100 = Rs. 400

CI = P[(1 + R/100)n - 1]

⇒ 1000[(1 + 10/100)⁴ - 1]

⇒ 1000[14641/10000 - 1]

⇒ 1000 × 4641/10000 = Rs 464.10

Now, Difference = 464.1 - 400 = Rs. 64.10

**∴ Option (4) is the correct answer.**

questions.question: The average of 11 numbers is 7.5. What should be the 12th number added to them to make the average 8.5?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Average of 11 numbers: 7.5

Desired average after adding the 12th number: 8.5

**Concept:**

The 12th number can be found by multiplying the desired average by 12 and then subtracting the sum of the first 11 numbers.

**Solution:**

Sum of first 11 numbers = 7.5 × 11 ⇒ 82.5

12th number = 8.5 × 12 - 82.5 ⇒ 19.5

**Therefore, the 12th number should be 19.5 to make the average 8.5.**

questions.question: Find the greatest number that will divide 57, 93 and 191 so as to leave the same remainder in each case.
questions.solution:
**Given**

Numbers: 57, 93, 191

**Concept:**

The greatest number that leaves the same remainder when dividing multiple numbers is the greatest common divisor (GCD) of the differences between those numbers.

**Calculation:**

Find the differences between the numbers ⇒ 93 - 57 = 36, 191 - 93 = 98

The GCD of 36 and 98 is 2

**Therefore, the greatest number that will divide 57, 93 and 191 so as to leave the same remainder in each case is 2.**

questions.question: What will be the total amount payable on a sum of Rs. 12,500 after two years at the rate of 10% per annum if the interest is compounded annually?
questions.solution:

Effective rate of compound interest for 2 years at 10% = 10% + 10% + (10 × 10) ÷ 100% = 21%

Total amount payable after 2 years = Principal × (100% + 21%)

⇒ Total Amount = 121% of 12500

⇒ Total Amount = 1.21 × 12500 = 15125

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 15,125.**

questions.question: Ram completes a work in 8 days, Rahim in 16 days and Shyam in 12 days. If all three work together, then in how many days will half of work complete?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Let, the total time required in days = m

⇒ dfrac{1}{m} = dfrac{1}{8} + dfrac{1}{16} + dfrac{1}{12}

⇒ dfrac{1}{m} = dfrac{6 + 3 + 4}{48} = dfrac{13}{48}

⇒ Half work time = dfrac{m}{2} = dfrac{48}{13 times 2}

⇒ Required Time = 1dfrac{11}{13} days

**∴ The Half work completion would require 1**dfrac{11}{13}** days.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** 

 

In the question, it is asked that → If all three work together, then in how many days **HALF OF THE WORK** will be completed?

 

Let the total work be 48 units (LCM of 8, 16 and 12)

 

Thus, Half Work = 24 units

 

⇒ Efficiency of Ram = 48/8 = 6 units/day

 

⇒ Efficiency of Rahim = 48/16 = 3 units/day

 

⇒ Efficiency of Shyam = 48/12 = 4 units/day

 

Their combined efficiency = 13

 

Thus the time required = 24/13 = 1 (11)/(13) days

questions.question: When x is subtracted from each of 25, 32, 59 and 80, the numbers so obtained, in this order, are proportional. What is the mean proportional between (3x + 1) and (5x - 4)?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Find the difference between the pairs: **(32 − 25) = 7** and **(80 − 59) = 21**.

The ratio of differences is **7 : 21 = 1 : 3**.

Apply the cross-multiplication shortcut for x: **x = |(3 × 25 − 1 × 59) / (3 − 1)| = |(75 − 59) / 2| = 8**.

Mean proportional between **(3 × 8 + 1) = 25** and **(5 × 8 − 4) = 36** is **√(25 × 36)**.

Result = **5 × 6 = 30**.

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The numbers **25, 32, 59, 80** become proportional when **x** is subtracted from each.

**Formula:** If a, b, c, d are in proportion, then **a/b = c/d**. Mean proportional of m and n is **√(m × n)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d53c48d90780e1b56081e0afb8263811e2f63ca3f3faf7d80a7852089f09db7a.png] 

⇒ **(25 − x) / (32 − x) = (59 − x) / (80 − x)**

⇒ **(25 − x)(80 − x) = (59 − x)(32 − x)**

⇒ **2000 − 25x − 80x + x² = 1888 − 59x − 32x + x²**

⇒ **2000 − 105x = 1888 − 91x**

⇒ **2000 − 1888 = 105x − 91x**

⇒ **112 = 14x**

⇒ **x = 8**

Now, finding the **Mean Proportional** between **(3x + 1)** and **(5x − 4)**:

⇒ **Term 1 = 3(8) + 1 = 25**

⇒ **Term 2 = 5(8) − 4 = 36**

⇒ **Mean Proportional = √(25 × 36) = 5 × 6 = 30**

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

**__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers **a** and **b** is the value **x** such that **a/x = x/b**, calculated as **x = √(ab)**.

Third Proportional

For two numbers **a** and **b**, the third proportional **c** is such that **a : b :: b : c**, calculated as **c = b²/a**.

Fourth Proportional

For three numbers **a, b,** and **c**, the fourth proportional **d** is such that **a : b :: c : d**, calculated as **d = (b × c) / a**.

Componendo and Dividendo

If **a/b = c/d**, then **(a + b)/(a − b) = (c + d)/(c − d)**, which is often used to simplify ratio-based equations.</p

questions.question: Somu has borrowed ₹10,000 from a money lender with simple interest at a rate of 7% half yearly. How much amount will he pay to the money lender after 3 years?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sum = Rs. 10000, Time = 3 years 

Rate of interest = 7% half-yearly

**Formula used:**

S.I = (P × T × R)/100

Amount = P + S.I

Here, P = Principle, T = time, R = rate

**Calculation:**

When interest is taken half yearly,

Actual rate of interest = 2 × rate of interest 

∴ R = 7 × 2 = 14%

Now, S.I = (10000 × 3 × 14)/100 = Rs. 4200

So, amount after 3 years = 10000 + 4200 = Rs. 14200

**∴ He will pay Rs. 14200 to the money lender after 3 years.**

if we take time in years then the rate per year is 7 x 2 = 14 %

if we take time in a half-year format then time = 3 x 2 = 6

questions.question: A trader marked the price of an article so as to earn a profit of 28% on its cost price. He sold it by giving 15% discount on its marked price. What was his actual profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Successive Percentage** formula: Net % = x + y + (xy/100)

Mark-up (x) = +28% | Discount (y) = −15%

Actual Profit % = 28 − 15 + [28 × (−15) / 100]

Actual Profit % = 13 − 4.2 = 8.8%

**∴ The correct answer is 8.8%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Mark-up over cost price = 28%, Discount on marked price = 15%.

**Formula Used:** Profit % = [(Selling Price − Cost Price) / Cost Price] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4404ca222935ef8730f08c731afc3207701be432473c82d89a78b5cb6b9345da.png] 

⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of the article be ₹100.

⇒ Since the **Marked Price (MP)** is set to earn 28% profit over CP:

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + (28/100) × 100 = ₹128.

⇒ A **Discount** of 15% is given on the **Marked Price**:

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = MP − 15% of MP

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 128 − (15/100) × 128 = 128 − 19.2

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = ₹108.8.

⇒ **Actual Profit** = SP − CP = 108.8 − 100 = ₹8.8.

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (8.8 / 100) × 100 = 8.8%.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.8%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between CP and MP

The relationship is given by the formula: MP / CP = (100 + Profit%) / (100 − Discount%).

Net Profit for Successive Changes

When a value is increased by a% and then decreased by b%, the net change is [a − b − (ab/100)]%.

Mark-up Percentage

Mark-up % = [(MP − CP) / CP] × 100. It is the percentage by which the cost price is raised to fix the marked price.

questions.question: A can complete a job in 26 days. If B is 30% more efficient than A, how many days will B alone take to complete the same job?
questions.solution:
Given:

The number of days taken by A to complete the job = 26

The efficiency of B is 30% more than A.

Concept used,

If someone completes work in x days

Work done in 1 day = 1/x part of the work

Calculation

B is 30% more efficient than A

The ratio of number of days taken by A to B = 130 ∶ 100 = 13∶10

Let B takes X number of days.

⇒ 26 ∶ X ∶ ∶ 13 ∶ 10

⇒ 13X = 260

⇒ X = 260/13

⇒ X = 20

∴ The number of days taken by B alone = 20 days

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] __Important Points__

Working efficiency is the work done by an individual in one day and this efficiency is inversely proportional to the number of days to complete a work.

It means that a person who takes fewer days to complete a work is said to be more efficient than a person who takes more days to complete the same work.

Hence we can reject options 1 and 4 as they are greater than 26 days.

questions.question: The average weight of an apple in a sample of 10 apples was calculated as 104 g. Later on, it was found that the weighing had shown the weight of each apple 20 g less. The correct average weight of an apple in that sample is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If each value in a data set is increased by a constant amount, the **average** of the set increases by that same amount.

Since each of the **10 apples** was **20 g** lighter than its actual weight, the **average** is also **20 g** less than the actual average.

Correct Average = Recorded Average + Error per apple

Correct Average = 104 + 20 = 124 g

**∴ The correct answer is 124 g.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of apples = 10

Observed average weight = 104 g

Weight error per apple = −20 g (under-weighed)

**Formula Used:**

Total Weight = Average Weight × Number of items

Correct Average = Correct Total Weight ÷ Number of items

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/935bffc6a146b09c4ec63d40420d091cd4408583bc67be8f20c461daa313a85f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total observed weight of 10 apples = 104 × 10 = 1040 g

⇒ Total weight error = 20 × 10 = 200 g

⇒ Actual total weight = 1040 + 200 = 1240 g

⇒ Actual average weight = 1240 ÷ 10 = 124 g

**∴ The correct answer is 124 g.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effect of Arithmetic Operations on Average

If every observation in a data set is increased, decreased, multiplied, or divided by a constant **k**, the **mean (average)** of the data set also increases, decreases, is multiplied, or divided by **k** respectively.

Correcting the Average Formula

Correct Average = [ (Observed Average × n) + (Actual value − Wrong value) ] ÷ n. This formula is useful when specific values are misread or miscalculated.

Sum of Observations

The sum of **n** observations is equal to the product of the **average** and the number of observations (**Sum = Average × n**).</p

questions.question: A trader offers a discount of 10% on an article if a customer makes the payment in cash. How much percentage above the cost price should he mark the article to make a profit of 10%? [Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.]
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct relationship formula: **MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%)**.

Ratio MP : CP = (100 + 10) : (100 − 10) = 110 : 90 = 11 : 9.

Marked-up value = 11 − 9 = 2 units.

**Markup percentage** = (2 ÷ 9) × 100 = 22.22%.

**∴ The correct answer is 22.22%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Discount = 10%, Profit = 10%.

**Formulas:** SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100 | SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100 | Markup% = (MP − CP) ÷ CP × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/886d79bcea70f1f44bcf95e6ed2621cc032246c772df25fefa61be6805f955f9.png] 

⇒ Let **Cost Price (CP)** = 100.

⇒ Since Profit is 10%, **Selling Price (SP)** = 100 + 10 = 110.

⇒ This SP is obtained after a 10% discount on **Marked Price (MP)**. So, 0.90 × MP = 110.

⇒ MP = 110 ÷ 0.90 = 1100 ÷ 9 = 122.22.

⇒ Markup Percentage = ((122.22 − 100) ÷ 100) × 100 = 22.22%.

**∴ The correct answer is 22.22%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between MP and CP

The ratio of **Marked Price** to **Cost Price** can always be expressed as (100 + Profit%) / (100 − Discount%).

Marked Price vs Selling Price

**Marked Price** is the price printed on the label, while **Selling Price** is the final amount paid after deducting the **Discount**.</p

questions.question: Reflection of the point (2, 3) on the X-axis is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **reflection** of any point (x, y) across the **X-axis**, follow this rule:

Keep the **x-coordinate** exactly the same and change the sign of the **y-coordinate**.

Rule: (x, y) → (x, −y)

Applying to (2, 3):

Keep 2 as is, and change 3 to −3.

**∴ The correct answer is (2, −3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Coordinates of the original point = (2, 3)

Axis of reflection = **X-axis**

**Formula Used:**

If a point P(x, y) is reflected in the **X-axis**, its image P'(x', y') is given by:

x' = x

y' = −y

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/61a34c4d807d88a73c93b5260d1b2738b131e7871fd0abf826496faac4c5c47c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ The original point is (x, y) = (2, 3).

⇒ In a reflection across the **horizontal axis** (X-axis), the point moves vertically to the opposite side of the axis.

⇒ The distance of the point from the X-axis is 3 units (the y-coordinate).

⇒ The reflected point will also be 3 units away from the X-axis but in the opposite (negative) direction.

⇒ Therefore, the new y-coordinate = −3.

⇒ The x-coordinate remains unchanged as the reflection is vertical.

⇒ New coordinates = (2, −3).

**∴ The correct answer is (2, −3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Reflection in Y-axis

When reflecting a point (x, y) across the **Y-axis**, the y-coordinate remains the same and the x-coordinate changes sign: (x, y) → (−x, y).

Reflection in Origin

When reflecting a point (x, y) through the **Origin (0,0)**, both coordinates change their signs: (x, y) → (−x, −y).

Reflection in line y = x

When reflecting a point (x, y) across the line **y = x**, the coordinates are swapped: (x, y) → (y, x).</p

questions.question: A person travels from A to B at a speed of 30 km/h and returns at a speed of 45 km/h. What is the average speed in km/h during the whole journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the **distance** traveled is the **same** for both speeds, apply the harmonic mean formula.

Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

Average Speed = (2 × 30 × 45) ÷ (30 + 45) = 2700 ÷ 75 = 36 kmph.

**∴ The correct answer is 36 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3abf91e0e45aa5f34ae5e42162b5c2d3d432eece71fba89bdcf694100fad70e1.png] 

**Given:**

Speed from A to B (S₁) = 30 km/h

Speed from B to A (S₂) = 45 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the distance between A and B be the **LCM** of 30 and 45 = 90 km.

⇒ Time taken from A to B (T₁) = 90 ÷ 30 = 3 hours.

⇒ Time taken from B to A (T₂) = 90 ÷ 45 = 2 hours.

⇒ Total Distance = 90 + 90 = 180 km.

⇒ Total Time = 3 + 2 = 5 hours.

⇒ Average Speed = 180 ÷ 5 = 36 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 36 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Time

If a person travels at different speeds for **equal time intervals**, the average speed is the **Arithmetic Mean**: (S₁ + S₂) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in **opposite directions**, relative speed = S₁ + S₂. In the **same direction**, relative speed = |S₁ − S₂|.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: Akhil can complete a piece of work in 26 days. Sakshi and Akhil both can complete the same work in 20 days. They started together but Sakshi left after working for 6 days. Find the number of days in which Akhil will complete the remaining work.
questions.solution:
**Given**

Akhil can complete work in 26 days

Akhil and Sakshi can complete work in 20 days

Sakshi left the work after 6 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

Let the total work be 260 units (LCM of 20 and 26)

⇒ Efficiency of Akhil = 260/26 = 10 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of Akhil and Sakshi = 260/20 = 13 units/day

Work done by Akhil and Sakshi in 6 days = 13 × 6 = 78 units

Remaining work = 260 - 78 = 182 units

Time taken by Akhil to complete remaining work = 182/10 = 91/5 days

**∴ Akhil will complete the remaining work in 91/5 days.**

questions.question: Three partners A, B and C started a business. A invested 1/3 of the total capital, B invested 60% of the remaining capital and C invested the rest. At the end of a year, the total profit was Rs. 18 lakhs. What is the difference between the shares of profit of A and C?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let total capital = 15 units (LCM of 3 and 5).

A = 1/3 × 15 = 5 units.

Remaining = 10 units → B = 60% of 10 = 6 units → C = 10 − 6 = 4 units.

Ratio A : B : C = 5 : 6 : 4. Total = 15 units.

Difference (A − C) = 5 − 4 = 1 unit.

Value = (1 ÷ 15) × 18,00,000 = Rs. 1,20,000.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,20,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Profit = Rs. 18,00,000

A's investment share = 1/3

B's investment share = 60% of (1 − 1/3)

**Formula:** Profit share ∝ Investment × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ad4b0d8d6818147bf0d2dbbdb65f2af6cffb7f825c75c116d44fad6245d12434.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total investment = 1 unit

⇒ A = 1/3

⇒ Remaining = 1 − 1/3 = 2/3

⇒ B = 60/100 × 2/3 = 3/5 × 2/3 = 2/5

⇒ C = 2/3 − 2/5 = (10 − 6) ÷ 15 = 4/15

⇒ Ratio A : B : C = 1/3 : 2/5 : 4/15

⇒ Multiply by LCM (15) → 5 : 6 : 4

⇒ Total parts = 5 + 6 + 4 = 15

⇒ Difference between A and C = 5 − 4 = 1 part

⇒ Required difference = (1 ÷ 15) × 18,00,000

⇒ Difference = Rs. 1,20,000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,20,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit Sharing Principle

In a partnership, profit is always distributed in the ratio of the product of Investment (Capital) and Time period: Profit₁ : Profit₂ = (C₁ × T₁) : (C₂ × T₂).

Types of Partners

A working partner manages the business and may receive a fixed salary or percentage of profit before distribution, while a sleeping partner only invests capital.

Calculation of Individual Profit

Profit of a partner = (Partner ratio ÷ Sum of all ratios) × Total Profit.</p

questions.question: A policeman spots a thief at a distance of 200 m and starts chasing him. While the policeman runs at a speed of 9 km/h, the thief runs at a speed of 7 km/h. After how long will the policeman catch the thief?
questions.solution:
Given:

Distance(d) = 200 m

Speed of the policeman(b) = 9 km/h

Speed of the thief(a) = 7 km/h

Formula Used :

(i) Time = d ÷ [(b - a)]

Calculations:

d = 200 m ,

⇒ a = 7 km/h = 7 × 5/18 = 35/18 m/s

⇒ b = 9 km/h = 9 × 5/18 = 5/2 m/s

According to the formula

Time = d ÷ (b - a)

Time = 200 ÷ (5/2 – 35/18)

Time = (200)/(frac{10){18}}

Time = 18 × 20

Time = 360 s = 360/60 = 6 minutes

Hence, The Police will take 6 minutes to catch thief.

questions.question: A man covers 250 km, 120 km and 50 km at the speed of 50 km/h, k km/h and 25 km/h, respectively. If his average speed for the whole journey is 42 km/h, then what is the value of k?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance = 250 + 120 + 50 = 420 km.

Total time needed = Total distance ÷ Average speed = 420 ÷ 42 = 10 hours.

Time for first and third parts = (250 ÷ 50) + (50 ÷ 25) = 5 + 2 = 7 hours.

Time for second part = 10 − 7 = 3 hours.

Value of k = Distance ÷ Time = 120 ÷ 3 = 40 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distances: d₁ = 250 km, d₂ = 120 km, d₃ = 50 km

Speeds: v₁ = 50 km/h, v₂ = k km/h, v₃ = 25 km/h

Average Speed = 42 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 
•

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 250 + 120 + 50 = 420 km

⇒ Total Time = Total Distance ÷ Average Speed

⇒ Total Time = 420 ÷ 42 = 10 hours

⇒ Time for segment 1 (t₁) = 250 ÷ 50 = 5 hours

⇒ Time for segment 3 (t₃) = 50 ÷ 25 = 2 hours

⇒ Time for segment 2 (t₂) = Total Time − (t₁ + t₃)

⇒ t₂ = 10 − (5 + 2) = 3 hours

⇒ Speed of segment 2 (k) = Distance₂ ÷ t₂

⇒ k = 120 ÷ 3 = 40 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Two Equal Distances

If a person covers two equal distances at speeds x and y, then Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

If three equal distances are covered at speeds x, y, and z, then Average Speed = 3xyz ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Speed Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.</p
